expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.002 to 0.008 because a dot product can represent user-specific video preferences that additive ID biases cannot.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.006 if the learned affinity promotes relevant videos into each user's top five; it may be smaller than the GAUC movement.

candidates.rationale: The current additive scorer has usable within-user discrimination (GAUC 0.66891), but its global nDCG@5 is lower (0.53696); a personalized user-video affinity can alter relative item order within each user rather than only calibrating global effects.
candidates.text: Replace additive ID weights with a low-rank user-video dot-product scorer while retaining additive tab, hour, and weekday residuals.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, append one train-fitted categorical feature representing the pair (video_id, tab), with an explicit unknown bucket; retain all existing features, additive scoring, BCE loss, optimizer schedule, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.004 if videos have tab-specific relevance not captured by their global ID weight.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.002 to 0.006 if the interaction corrects top-five ordering in the weak tab slices; rare pairs may limit the global effect.

candidates.rationale: Request context was the only positively screened feature family (+0.00221 internal primary lift), while official validation shows especially poor context-specific ranking for tab 0 (nDCG@5 0.06219) and tab 8 (0.02634).
candidates.text: Add a single train-fitted video-ID-by-tab interaction to the existing additive scorer.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, replace the additive linear scorer with train-fitted embeddings for user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday followed by one MLP scalar head; keep exactly the same fields, BCE objective, temporal split, optimizer family, batch size, and early-stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.007 if nonlinear ID/context combinations improve within-user pair ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.006 if nonlinear scores resolve top-five ties and misorders; overfitting could instead leave it flat or reduce it.

candidates.rationale: The current model establishes that the permitted ID plus request-context fields carry signal, but its additive form cannot model nonlinear user-item-context combinations. The evidence supports retaining context and targeting within-user top-five ordering.
candidates.text: Replace the additive scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP ranker over the same permitted ID and request-context fields.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, replace the additive scorer with an embedding MLP augmented by exactly one explicit cross layer over embeddings for user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday; keep the fields, BCE loss, temporal split, and early-stopping policy unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.006 if one bounded cross layer captures context-dependent item preference.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.002 to 0.007 if the cross layer improves candidate ordering in weak context slices; it can decline if sparse combinations are memorized.

candidates.rationale: The strongest observed weakness is heterogeneous request context, especially tab-specific top-five quality, which is a plausible setting for bounded ID-by-context interactions without adding any new feature family.
candidates.text: Add a one-layer explicit cross branch to an embedding MLP over the current permitted fields.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, replace BCE with a deterministic RankNet logistic pair loss over positive-negative training rows belonging to the same user, with equal user weighting and no cross-user pairs; keep features, additive model, optimizer schedule, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.002 to 0.007 because the loss directly trains within-user positive-negative score margins.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.004; it improves only if the sampled pair corrections concentrate near the top five.

candidates.rationale: The official objective is within-user GAUC plus nDCG@5, whereas experiment 1 optimizes pointwise BCE. GAUC is relatively stronger than nDCG@5, so directly optimizing positive-versus-negative ordering is a high-information objective test.
candidates.text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-user RankNet pairwise loss using only training rows grouped by user.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, change the loss from BCE alone to BCE plus a deterministic within-user positive-negative logistic term weighted by detached absolute nDCG@5 swap gain; keep the additive model, features, optimizer schedule, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.001 to +0.004 because focusing updates near rank five may sacrifice some broad pair ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.002 to 0.008 if positives just below rank five are promoted above top-five negatives.

candidates.rationale: Experiment 1 has global GAUC 0.66891 but nDCG@5 0.53696, and rare items show GAUC 0.60000 with nDCG@5 only 0.17174. This metric separation motivates a narrowly top-rank-focused loss change.
candidates.text: Add an nDCG@5-weighted pairwise term to the existing BCE objective.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, replace row-mean BCE with BCE weighted by the inverse number of training rows for each user, with weights computed from the training split only; keep features, additive model, optimizer schedule, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.005 if equal user influence better matches the within-user GAUC target.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.003 because pointwise reweighting does not directly target top-five positions.

candidates.rationale: The evaluated objective is within-user, while the current minibatch BCE gives users with more rows more loss mass. The observed global GAUC demonstrates meaningful within-user ranking signal worth aligning with a user-balanced training reduction.
candidates.text: Use user-normalized pointwise BCE instead of row-averaged BCE.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, change only l2 from 0.000001 to 0.00001; retain model, features, BCE loss, learning rate, batch size, split, seed, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.001 to +0.003; shrinkage may improve generalization but can underfit established ID preferences.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.003; reducing extreme sparse-ID scores may improve top-five stability, but the effect is uncertain.

candidates.rationale: The current model includes high-cardinality user and video ID weights and has weak rare-item top-five performance, a setting where stronger shrinkage can reduce unstable sparse-ID estimates without introducing new data or features.
candidates.text: Increase only L2 regularization of the existing additive model by one order of magnitude.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, change only learning_rate from 0.01 to 0.003; retain features, additive model, BCE loss, L2, batch size, maximum epochs, seed, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.001 to +0.003; a smaller step can improve convergence precision but may undertrain under the fixed epoch budget.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.003; any gain requires improved score ordering rather than merely lower pointwise loss.

candidates.rationale: Experiment 1 is the sole scored reference and achieved a viable primary score of 0.60293; a lower learning rate is a clean optimization-stability control before allocating budget to a more complex model.
candidates.text: Reduce only the learning rate of the existing additive model from 0.01 to 0.003.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, change only max_epochs from 10 to 20; retain model, fields, BCE loss, optimizer hyperparameters, seed, patience, validation proxy, and splits unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by 0.000 to +0.003 if the original run was not converged; patience may make the realized training duration unchanged.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.003; later epochs can improve ordering or overfit the proxy-selected checkpoint.

candidates.rationale: The current experiment uses only ten maximum epochs and stops on a GAUC proxy, while the official objective also includes nDCG@5. Extending the budget while retaining the same patience is a bounded test of whether optimization is prematurely capped.
candidates.text: Increase only the maximum training epoch budget for the existing additive model from 10 to 20.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, append one train-fitted categorical feature representing the pair (video_id, hour), with an explicit unknown bucket; retain existing fields, additive scoring, BCE loss, optimizer schedule, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.004 if time-specific item preferences correct within-user comparisons.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.005 if the interaction improves top-five ordering in weak hour slices; sparsity can make the global effect negligible.

candidates.rationale: Request context had full coverage and positive train-only lift, while multiple hour slices have materially weak nDCG@5, including hour 3 at 0.38637 and hour 16 at 0.35704. Item relevance may differ by time of day.
candidates.text: Add a single train-fitted video-ID-by-hour interaction to the existing additive scorer.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, replace the additive scorer with a rank-d factorization machine over exactly user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday, including its standard linear terms; keep BCE loss, optimizer schedule, temporal split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.002 to 0.008 if compact user-video and video-context interactions improve pairwise ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.007 if those interactions reorder candidates near rank five; extra capacity may instead overfit sparse field pairs.

candidates.rationale: The current additive model cannot express any pairwise interaction among user, video, tab, hour, and weekday. Request context is the only screened feature family with positive lift, making a compact interaction model more defensible than adding rejected feature families.
candidates.text: Replace scalar user and video ID weights with a second-order factorization-machine interaction over all current categorical fields.

ranking.rationale: Best scarce-run tradeoff: directly tests the largest structural limitation of additive user/item biases—absence of personalized user-video relative preferences—while retaining the screened context residuals. It is a clean, low-runtime architectural ablation with broad applicability and low leakage risk. Evidence is indirect rather than an observed interaction lift, so confidence is moderate, but it is less validation-slice-specific and less capacity-heavy than the other interaction models.

A narrowly scoped, cheap interaction that preserves the successful baseline and targets the only positively screened feature family. Large tab-0 volume makes this more credible than its small tab-8 slice alone. Penalized because the claimed tab-specific benefit relies partly on retrospective validation slices and because sparse video-tab pairs may mostly memorize rather than generalize.

Similar low-risk incremental interaction test to c02, with hour slices providing some motivation and full request-context coverage. It ranks below video-tab because hour has 24 values, creating materially more sparse video-context pairs, and the cited weak-hour diagnostics are weaker and more diffuse than the tab evidence.

Strong objective alignment with within-user GAUC and a clean single-axis loss ablation. It avoids cross-user pairs and leakage, but its expected nDCG@5 effect is uncertain, pair construction increases runtime and optimization sensitivity, and the cited rare-item slice is weak evidence for a global loss change.

A compact model that preserves linear terms while testing user-video and context interactions, avoiding the information loss in c01's replacement of ID biases. However, it simultaneously enables every pairwise field interaction, making attribution broad, sparse-pair overfitting more likely, and runtime/tuning risk higher for one experiment.

Very clean and inexpensive alignment of pointwise training mass with the within-user evaluation unit. It has low leakage and implementation risk, but only indirect evidence, no direct top-k optimization, and a small projected gain; it is a sensible conservative fallback rather than the highest-upside scarce run.

Tests meaningful nonlinear user-item-context effects using permitted fields, but it is a broad replacement rather than a minimal ablation. The MLP confounds embeddings, nonlinear architecture, and capacity; with only one scored reference, its moderate runtime and overfitting risks outweigh its plausible upside.

The metric gap gives this a reasonable top-rank hypothesis, but detached nDCG swap gains derived from current scores add substantial implementation and optimization complexity. Its motivation leans heavily on retrospective validation slices, creating validation-overfitting risk, and it overlaps substantially with c05 while being less interpretable and less robust.

Potentially expressive for context-dependent preferences, but it combines embedding replacement, MLP capacity, and explicit crosses in one broad ablation. This duplicates the interaction objectives of c03 and c12 with lower feasibility, greater tuning burden, and stronger sparse-combination memorization risk.

Low-cost regularization control with a plausible sparse-ID rationale, but the one-order-of-magnitude setting is arbitrary and evidence does not establish overfitting in the baseline. Its projected gain is small and it is unlikely to resolve the core missing-interaction limitation.

A bounded protocol check, but there is no convergence evidence supporting a larger epoch cap, and unchanged patience may make the experiment operationally identical. It risks selecting a checkpoint against an incomplete GAUC proxy rather than improving the official composite ranking objective.

Clean and cheap but weakest hypothesis: no learning-curve, instability, or nonconvergence evidence supports the proposed rate. It has low novelty, low expected gain, and may simply undertrain under the fixed schedule, making it poor use of the sole experiment.

warnings: Segments are diagnostic slices of official validation, not independent test estimates.

response.selection_rationale: Select c01. It is the consultant's top-ranked option (utility 0.79) and directly addresses the baseline's principal structural limitation: additive user and video biases cannot alter relative video ordering according to personalized user-video affinity. It retains the only positively screened context fields and their additive residuals, making the ablation focused and interpretable. Its expected primary gain is among the highest (0.004), with moderate confidence, low leakage risk, and low runtime risk. This offers a more broadly applicable and reliable improvement test than validation-slice-targeted sparse interactions, while avoiding the higher tuning, attribution, and overfitting risks of MLP, cross-network, and factorization-machine alternatives.

"""Train the neutral seed scaffold and emit validation scores for fixed evaluation."""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from data import encode, load
from model import Model


def within_user_auc(user_ids, labels, scores):
    """Training-only early-stop proxy; final scoring is owned by the Experimentor."""
    grouped = {}
    for user, label, score in zip(user_ids, labels, scores):
        grouped.setdefault(str(user), []).append((float(score), int(label)))
    numerator = denominator = 0.0
    for rows in grouped.values():
        positives = sum(label for _, label in rows)
        negatives = len(rows) - positives
        if positives == 0 or negatives == 0:
            continue
        wins = 0.0
        for positive_score, label in rows:
            if not label:
                continue
            for negative_score, other_label in rows:
                if other_label:
                    continue
                wins += positive_score > negative_score
                wins += 0.5 * (positive_score == negative_score)
        numerator += positives * wins / (positives * negatives)
        denominator += positives
    return numerator / denominator if denominator else 0.5


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--contract-check", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with open(args.config, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        config = json.load(handle)
    splits = load(args.data_dir, max_rows_per_split=64 if args.contract_check else None)
    encoded, dimension = encode(splits)
    train_features, train_labels, _ = encoded["train"]
    valid_features, valid_labels, valid_users = encoded["valid"]
    test_features, _ = encoded["test"]
    model = Model(
        dimension,
        learning_rate=config["learning_rate"],
        l2=config["l2"],
    )
    if args.contract_check:
        probe_size = min(8, len(train_labels))
        if probe_size == 0 or len(valid_labels) == 0:
            raise ValueError("contract probe requires non-empty train and validation slices")
        loss = model.step(train_features[:probe_size], train_labels[:probe_size])
        probe_scores = model.predict(valid_features[:probe_size])
        if probe_scores.ndim != 1 or len(probe_scores) != min(probe_size, len(valid_features)):
            raise ValueError("model prediction shape violates the interface contract")
        if not np.isfinite(loss) or not np.all(np.isfinite(probe_scores)):
            raise ValueError("model produced NaN or infinity during contract probe")
        print(json.dumps({"contract": "ok", "feature_shape": list(train_features.shape)}))
        return
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config["seed"])
    best_score, best_state, stale = -1.0, None, 0
    for epoch in range(1, config["max_epochs"] + 1):
        order = rng.permutation(len(train_labels))
        losses = []
        for index in range(0, len(order), config["batch_size"]):
            batch = order[index:index + config["batch_size"]]
            losses.append(model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch]))
        predictions = model.predict(valid_features)
        proxy = within_user_auc(valid_users, valid_labels, predictions)
        print(f"epoch={epoch} loss={np.mean(losses):.6f} valid_gauc_proxy={proxy:.6f}")
        if proxy > best_score + 1e-5:
            best_score, best_state, stale = proxy, model.state(), 0
        else:
            stale += 1
            if stale >= config["patience"]:
                break
    if best_state is None:
        raise RuntimeError("training produced no checkpoint")
    model.load_state(best_state)
    output_dir = Path(args.output)
    np.savez(
        output_dir.with_name("predictions_valid.npz"),
        row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_features), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(valid_features),
    )
    np.savez(
        output_dir.with_name("predictions_test.npz"),
        row_ids=np.arange(len(test_features), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(test_features),
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Low-rank user-video interaction model with categorical residuals."""

import numpy as np


def sigmoid(value):
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(value, -30, 30)))


class Model:
    def __init__(self, dimension, learning_rate=0.01, l2=1e-6):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
        self.user_embeddings = rng.normal(
            0.0, 0.01, size=(dimension, 16)
        ).astype(np.float32)
        self.video_embeddings = rng.normal(
            0.0, 0.01, size=(dimension, 16)
        ).astype(np.float32)
        self.residual_weights = np.zeros(dimension, dtype=np.float32)
        self.bias = np.float32(0.0)
        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        self.l2 = l2

        self.user_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        self.user_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        self.video_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        self.video_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        self.residual_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)
        self.residual_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)
        self.step_number = 0

    @staticmethod
    def _normalized_interaction(user_vectors, video_vectors):
        epsilon = np.float32(1e-8)
        user_norms = np.sqrt((user_vectors * user_vectors).sum(axis=1) + epsilon)
        video_norms = np.sqrt((video_vectors * video_vectors).sum(axis=1) + epsilon)
        user_hat = user_vectors / user_norms[:, None]
        video_hat = video_vectors / video_norms[:, None]
        dots = (user_hat * video_hat).sum(axis=1)
        return dots, user_hat, video_hat, user_norms, video_norms

    def logits(self, features):
        user_vectors = self.user_embeddings[features[:, 0]]
        video_vectors = self.video_embeddings[features[:, 1]]
        interaction, _, _, _, _ = self._normalized_interaction(
            user_vectors, video_vectors
        )
        residual = self.residual_weights[features[:, 2:5]].sum(axis=1)
        return self.bias + interaction + residual

    def _adam_update(self, parameter, gradient, first_moment, second_moment):
        beta1, beta2, epsilon = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
        first_moment *= beta1
        first_moment += (1 - beta1) * gradient
        second_moment *= beta2
        second_moment += (1 - beta2) * (gradient * gradient)
        first_hat = first_moment / (1 - beta1 ** self.step_number)
        second_hat = second_moment / (1 - beta2 ** self.step_number)
        parameter -= self.learning_rate * first_hat / (np.sqrt(second_hat) + epsilon)

    def step(self, features, labels):
        size = len(labels)
        user_ids = features[:, 0]
        video_ids = features[:, 1]
        residual_ids = features[:, 2:5]

        user_vectors = self.user_embeddings[user_ids]
        video_vectors = self.video_embeddings[video_ids]
        interaction, user_hat, video_hat, user_norms, video_norms = (
            self._normalized_interaction(user_vectors, video_vectors)
        )
        residual = self.residual_weights[residual_ids].sum(axis=1)
        logits = self.bias + interaction + residual
        probabilities = sigmoid(logits)
        gradient = ((probabilities - labels) / size).astype(np.float32)

        grad_user_embeddings = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        grad_video_embeddings = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        grad_residual_weights = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)

        user_gradient = gradient[:, None] * (
            video_hat - interaction[:, None] * user_hat
        ) / user_norms[:, None]
        video_gradient = gradient[:, None] * (
            user_hat - interaction[:, None] * video_hat
        ) / video_norms[:, None]
        np.add.at(grad_user_embeddings, user_ids, user_gradient)
        np.add.at(grad_video_embeddings, video_ids, video_gradient)
        np.add.at(
            grad_residual_weights,
            residual_ids.ravel(),
            np.repeat(gradient, residual_ids.shape[1]),
        )

        grad_user_embeddings += self.l2 * self.user_embeddings
        grad_video_embeddings += self.l2 * self.video_embeddings
        grad_residual_weights += self.l2 * self.residual_weights

        self.step_number += 1
        self._adam_update(
            self.user_embeddings,
            grad_user_embeddings,
            self.user_first_moment,
            self.user_second_moment,
        )
        self._adam_update(
            self.video_embeddings,
            grad_video_embeddings,
            self.video_first_moment,
            self.video_second_moment,
        )
        self._adam_update(
            self.residual_weights,
            grad_residual_weights,
            self.residual_first_moment,
            self.residual_second_moment,
        )
        self.bias -= self.learning_rate * gradient.sum()

        return float(-np.mean(
            labels * np.log(probabilities + 1e-9)
            + (1 - labels) * np.log(1 - probabilities + 1e-9)
        ))

    def predict(self, features, batch_size=200_000):
        if len(features) == 0:
            return np.empty(0, dtype=np.float32)
        return np.concatenate([
            self.logits(features[index:index + batch_size])
            for index in range(0, len(features), batch_size)
        ])

    def state(self):
        return (
            self.user_embeddings.copy(),
            self.video_embeddings.copy(),
            self.residual_weights.copy(),

# Supplied KuaiRand-Pure files and official splits

## Summary and mechanism
The supplied data directory has three 19-column impression logs and three entity tables. ParLLiaMent's
official temporal split uses standard-exposure rows: train 2022-04-08 through 2022-04-21, validation
2022-04-22 through 2022-04-28, and test 2022-04-29 through 2022-05-08.

## When to use / avoid
Use this inventory before choosing data sources or defining temporal features. Avoid treating file
boundaries as split boundaries: the later standard log contains both validation and test dates.
Avoid treating the random-exposure file as official validation or test data.

## Requirements and implementation
Measured directly from the supplied CSVs: `log_standard_4_08_to_4_21_pure.csv` has 1,141,112 rows
covering 2022-04-09 through 2022-04-21; `log_standard_4_22_to_5_08_pure.csv` has 295,497 rows over 17
dates. Date filtering yields 124,909 validation rows and 170,588 test rows. The random log has
1,186,059 rows over 2022-04-22 through 2022-05-08. Entity tables contain 27,285 users and 7,583
videos, with one row per ID.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Read standard logs in source order, select rows by integer `date`, and preserve that order for
validation inference. Fit encoders and transforms on training only. Use explicit unknown buckets for
entities or values absent from training.

## Diagnostics and risks
The nominal train range includes April 8, but this supplied training file's observed minimum date is
April 9. Hard-coding expected daily row counts or concatenating all standard rows before fitting can
silently leak validation/test information. File names alone do not establish feature availability.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Before a run, assert filenames, headers, row counts, observed date bounds, unique IDs, and the exact
124,909-row validation selection. Fingerprint inputs so cached screening is invalidated after a data
change.

## Related cards and sources
See `dataset.interaction_log_schema`, `dataset.user_metadata`,
`dataset.video_metadata_and_statistics`, `dataset.random_exposure_log`, and
`task.prediction_artifact`. Counts were measured from the supplied KuaiRand-Pure CSVs; split rules
come from ParLLiaMent's fixed evaluator.

# Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics

## Summary and mechanism
GAUC summarizes per-user positive-negative ordering with positive-count weighting; nDCG@5 emphasizes
discounted relevance at the top five. Primary averages them.

## When to use / avoid
Use official metrics for selection and stopping. Use accuracy, precision, recall, F1, global AUC,
average precision, MAP@5, MRR@5, and HitRate@5 only to diagnose mechanisms.

## Requirements and implementation
Preserve canonical rows and group only inside fixed evaluation. Compare every change with its exact
parent and inspect segment support before interpreting deltas.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
No metric reweighting is permitted. A hypothesis should predict GAUC and nDCG@5 separately because
loss and sampling changes can trade them off.

## Diagnostics and risks
Validation-selected classification thresholds are optimistic. Score scaling can change thresholded
metrics without changing rank; zero-positive users make macro top-k metrics harsh but defined.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Run synthetic perfect, tied, all-negative, and non-finite cases before trusting evaluator changes.

## Related cards and sources
See `task.kuairand_ranking` and `experiment.scarce_budget`.
fixed_research_knowledge.title: Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics

# Counted-experiment and convergence protocol

## Summary and mechanism
ParLLiaMent has a scarce budget of at most 50 successfully scored experiments. The selected seed scaffold
is unscored parent 0. It may be the fresh simple scaffold or the optional KuaiRand FM baseline code,
but neither selection inserts a measured baseline result. Train-only screening, planning, failed
retries, and abandoned attempts do not receive experiment IDs or consume the counted budget.

## When to use / avoid
Use this card whenever prioritizing hypotheses or interpreting lineage. Prefer one high-information,
bounded change over broad searches. Avoid citing parent 0 as measured evidence, treating an
abandoned attempt as an experiment, or spending official experiments on basic schema discovery.

## Requirements and implementation
Only a successful validation score atomically becomes `experiment_N` and enters the Journal.
Generated candidates must reference parent 0 or an actually scored experiment available in the
current archive. One tournament winner proceeds to implementation per generation, even when draft
planning considered a larger candidate portfolio.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Before an official experiment, use the cached train-only temporal screen, literature, prior metrics,
and segment diagnostics to state one exact ablation and an expected effect on both GAUC and nDCG@5.
Reserve official scoring for changes with a plausible primary gain and a clean fallback.

## Diagnostics and risks
Every scored experiment with primary score `x` establishes a target of `x + 0.002`. ParLLiaMent stops if
all three subsequent scored experiments are strictly below that target, so the check requires at
least four scored experiments. Reaching the target in any of those three experiments prevents that
anchor from causing convergence. Abandoned attempts are absent from this sequence. The globally
highest-scoring validation experiment is selected for submission even when a later, lower-scoring
experiment triggers convergence. Repeated implementation failures waste wall-clock time despite
being uncounted.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Use profiling, train-only temporal holdout screening, contract checks, and code validation before
training. Then change the smallest coherent set of files needed for the winning hypothesis and
compare it against its declared scored parent.

## Related cards and sources
See `task.kuairand_ranking`, `task.prediction_artifact`, and
`evaluation.within_user_metrics`. The authoritative source is `parlliament_mle_plan.md` plus the
implemented Journal and Overseer convergence checks.
fixed_research_knowledge.title: Counted-experiment and convergence protocol

# KuaiRand within-user long-view ranking

## Summary and mechanism
The task scores the already logged impressions for each user; it is not full-catalog retrieval.
`long_view` is binary relevance. The official `primary` score is
`(GAUC + nDCG@5) / 2`, and it is the only experiment-selection and convergence objective.

## When to use / avoid
Use this card to reject changes that improve row calibration without changing within-user order.
Avoid treating the unscored seed or a user-only constant as a performance baseline.

## Requirements and implementation
Predictions must preserve canonical validation row order and contain one finite score per row. A
useful model must vary scores among a user's candidate items. GAUC is the positive-count-weighted
mean of per-user AUC over users containing both classes. nDCG@5 is macro-averaged over every user;
users with no positive impression receive zero nDCG.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Always report GAUC, nDCG@5, and primary separately. Optimize ordering, not a validation-selected
classification threshold. Classification and supplementary ranking metrics are diagnostic only.

## Diagnostics and risks
Global AUC can rise while GAUC stalls. Zero-positive users contribute zero nDCG but do not provide
within-user positive-negative AUC evidence. User-only constants cannot change within-user order;
user features need to interact with an item, author, context, or history signal to affect the score.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Before training, verify score variance within user and the exact prediction artifact contract. Test
one ranking-relevant change against a scored parent.

## Related cards and sources
See `task.experiment_protocol`, `task.prediction_artifact`,
`dataset.population_and_pair_shift`, and `evaluation.within_user_metrics`. Task details are fixed by
ParLLiaMent's immutable evaluator; dataset context is Gao et al., “KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential
Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos” (2022).
fixed_research_knowledge.title: KuaiRand within-user long-view ranking

# Impression-time availability and leakage policy

## Summary and mechanism
A feature is eligible only when its value would be known before ranking the target impression.
Historical aggregates must exclude the current label and all future events.

## When to use / avoid
Use timestamps, request context, and causally accumulated histories. Avoid current-impression
outcomes, official-validation-derived fitting, future histories, and snapshots lacking availability
timestamps.

## Requirements and implementation
Sort training events by time, compute features from prior state, then update state after emitting the
row. Fit vocabularies, thresholds, and transforms on training data only. Treat engagement columns
such as `is_click`, `play_time_ms`, and `long_view` as post-impression outcomes for the current row.
Treat the video-statistics snapshot as unavailable until its observation window is established.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Default unknown values explicitly and monitor coverage. Leakage can create implausibly large gains
in both GAUC and nDCG@5 that disappear under a temporal split.

## Diagnostics and risks
Warning signs are near-perfect metrics, cold rows outperforming warm rows unexpectedly, or gains
concentrated in post-event fields.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Perturb the current label and other current outcomes and verify the row's engineered features do not
change. Run the internal temporal holdout before an official experiment.

## Related cards and sources
See `dataset.interaction_log_schema`, `dataset.video_metadata_and_statistics`,
`features.causal_histories`, and `robustness.temporal_drift`.
fixed_research_knowledge.title: Impression-time availability and leakage policy

"""Train the neutral seed scaffold and emit validation scores for fixed evaluation."""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from data import encode, load
from model import Model


def within_user_auc(user_ids, labels, scores):
    """Training-only early-stop proxy; final scoring is owned by the Experimentor."""
    grouped = {}
    for user, label, score in zip(user_ids, labels, scores):
        grouped.setdefault(str(user), []).append((float(score), int(label)))
    numerator = denominator = 0.0
    for rows in grouped.values():
        positives = sum(label for _, label in rows)
        negatives = len(rows) - positives
        if positives == 0 or negatives == 0:
            continue
        wins = 0.0
        for positive_score, label in rows:
            if not label:
                continue
            for negative_score, other_label in rows:
                if other_label:
                    continue
                wins += positive_score > negative_score
                wins += 0.5 * (positive_score == negative_score)
        numerator += positives * wins / (positives * negatives)
        denominator += positives
    return numerator / denominator if denominator else 0.5


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--contract-check", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with open(args.config, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        config = json.load(handle)
    splits = load(args.data_dir, max_rows_per_split=64 if args.contract_check else None)
    encoded, dimension = encode(splits)
    train_features, train_labels, _ = encoded["train"]
    valid_features, valid_labels, valid_users = encoded["valid"]
    test_features, test_labels, _ = encoded["test"]
    model = Model(
        dimension,
        learning_rate=config["learning_rate"],
        l2=config["l2"],
    )
    if args.contract_check:
        probe_size = min(8, len(train_labels))
        if probe_size == 0 or len(valid_labels) == 0:
            raise ValueError("contract probe requires non-empty train and validation slices")
        loss = model.step(train_features[:probe_size], train_labels[:probe_size])
        probe_scores = model.predict(valid_features[:probe_size])
        if probe_scores.ndim != 1 or len(probe_scores) != min(probe_size, len(valid_features)):
            raise ValueError("model prediction shape violates the interface contract")
        if not np.isfinite(loss) or not np.all(np.isfinite(probe_scores)):
            raise ValueError("model produced NaN or infinity during contract probe")
        print(json.dumps({"contract": "ok", "feature_shape": list(train_features.shape)}))
        return
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config["seed"])
    best_score, best_state, stale = -1.0, None, 0
    for epoch in range(1, config["max_epochs"] + 1):
        order = rng.permutation(len(train_labels))
        losses = []
        for index in range(0, len(order), config["batch_size"]):
            batch = order[index:index + config["batch_size"]]
            losses.append(model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch]))
        predictions = model.predict(valid_features)
        proxy = within_user_auc(valid_users, valid_labels, predictions)
        print(f"epoch={epoch} loss={np.mean(losses):.6f} valid_gauc_proxy={proxy:.6f}")
        if proxy > best_score + 1e-5:
            best_score, best_state, stale = proxy, model.state(), 0
        else:
            stale += 1
            if stale >= config["patience"]:
                break
    if best_state is None:
        raise RuntimeError("training produced no checkpoint")
    model.load_state(best_state)
    np.savez(
        args.output,
        row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_labels), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(valid_features),
    )
    np.savez(
        Path(args.output).with_name("predictions_test.npz"),
        row_ids=np.arange(len(test_labels), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(test_features),
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Low-rank user-video interaction model with categorical residuals."""

import numpy as np


def sigmoid(value):
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(value, -30, 30)))


class Model:
    def __init__(self, dimension, learning_rate=0.01, l2=1e-6):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
        self.user_embeddings = rng.normal(
            0.0, 0.01, size=(dimension, 16)
        ).astype(np.float32)
        self.video_embeddings = rng.normal(
            0.0, 0.01, size=(dimension, 16)
        ).astype(np.float32)
        self.residual_weights = np.zeros(dimension, dtype=np.float32)
        self.bias = np.float32(0.0)
        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        self.l2 = l2

        self.user_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        self.user_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        self.video_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        self.video_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        self.residual_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)
        self.residual_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)
        self.step_number = 0

    @staticmethod
    def _normalized_interaction(user_vectors, video_vectors):
        epsilon = np.float32(1e-8)
        user_norms = np.sqrt((user_vectors * user_vectors).sum(axis=1) + epsilon)
        video_norms = np.sqrt((video_vectors * video_vectors).sum(axis=1) + epsilon)
        user_hat = user_vectors / user_norms[:, None]
        video_hat = video_vectors / video_norms[:, None]
        dots = (user_hat * video_hat).sum(axis=1)
        return dots, user_hat, video_hat, user_norms, video_norms

    def logits(self, features):
        user_vectors = self.user_embeddings[features[:, 0]]
        video_vectors = self.video_embeddings[features[:, 1]]
        interaction, _, _, _, _ = self._normalized_interaction(
            user_vectors, video_vectors
        )
        residual = self.residual_weights[features[:, 2:5]].sum(axis=1)
        return self.bias + interaction + residual

    def _adam_update(self, parameter, gradient, first_moment, second_moment):
        beta1, beta2, epsilon = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
        first_moment *= beta1
        first_moment += (1 - beta1) * gradient
        second_moment *= beta2
        second_moment += (1 - beta2) * (gradient * gradient)
        first_hat = first_moment / (1 - beta1 ** self.step_number)
        second_hat = second_moment / (1 - beta2 ** self.step_number)
        parameter -= self.learning_rate * first_hat / (np.sqrt(second_hat) + epsilon)

    def step(self, features, labels):
        size = len(labels)
        user_ids = features[:, 0]
        video_ids = features[:, 1]
        residual_ids = features[:, 2:5]

        user_vectors = self.user_embeddings[user_ids]
        video_vectors = self.video_embeddings[video_ids]
        interaction, user_hat, video_hat, user_norms, video_norms = (
            self._normalized_interaction(user_vectors, video_vectors)
        )
        residual = self.residual_weights[residual_ids].sum(axis=1)
        logits = self.bias + interaction + residual
        probabilities = sigmoid(logits)
        gradient = ((probabilities - labels) / size).astype(np.float32)

        grad_user_embeddings = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        grad_video_embeddings = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        grad_residual_weights = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)

        user_gradient = gradient[:, None] * (
            video_hat - interaction[:, None] * user_hat
        ) / user_norms[:, None]
        video_gradient = gradient[:, None] * (
            user_hat - interaction[:, None] * video_hat
        ) / video_norms[:, None]
        np.add.at(grad_user_embeddings, user_ids, user_gradient)
        np.add.at(grad_video_embeddings, video_ids, video_gradient)
        np.add.at(
            grad_residual_weights,
            residual_ids.ravel(),
            np.repeat(gradient, residual_ids.shape[1]),
        )

        grad_user_embeddings += self.l2 * self.user_embeddings
        grad_video_embeddings += self.l2 * self.video_embeddings
        grad_residual_weights += self.l2 * self.residual_weights

        self.step_number += 1
        self._adam_update(
            self.user_embeddings,
            grad_user_embeddings,
            self.user_first_moment,
            self.user_second_moment,
        )
        self._adam_update(
            self.video_embeddings,
            grad_video_embeddings,
            self.video_first_moment,
            self.video_second_moment,
        )
        self._adam_update(
            self.residual_weights,
            grad_residual_weights,
            self.residual_first_moment,
            self.residual_second_moment,
        )
        self.bias -= self.learning_rate * gradient.sum()

        return float(-np.mean(
            labels * np.log(probabilities + 1e-9)
            + (1 - labels) * np.log(1 - probabilities + 1e-9)
        ))

    def predict(self, features, batch_size=200_000):
        if len(features) == 0:
            return np.empty(0, dtype=np.float32)
        return np.concatenate([
            self.logits(features[index:index + batch_size])
            for index in range(0, len(features), batch_size)
        ])

    def state(self):
        return (
            self.user_embeddings.copy(),
            self.video_embeddings.copy(),
            self.residual_weights.copy(),
            np.float32(self.bias),
        )

    def load_state(self, state):
        user_embeddings, video_embeddings, residual_weights, bias = state
        self.user_embeddings = np.asarray(user_embeddings, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self.video_embeddings = np.asarray(video_embeddings, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self.residual_weights = np.asarray(residual_weights, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self.bias = np.float32(bias)

"""Train the neutral seed scaffold and emit validation scores for fixed evaluation."""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from data import encode, load
from model import Model


def within_user_auc(user_ids, labels, scores):
    """Training-only early-stop proxy; final scoring is owned by the Experimentor."""
    grouped = {}
    for user, label, score in zip(user_ids, labels, scores):
        grouped.setdefault(str(user), []).append((float(score), int(label)))
    numerator = denominator = 0.0
    for rows in grouped.values():
        positives = sum(label for _, label in rows)
        negatives = len(rows) - positives
        if positives == 0 or negatives == 0:
            continue
        wins = 0.0
        for positive_score, label in rows:
            if not label:
                continue
            for negative_score, other_label in rows:
                if other_label:
                    continue
                wins += positive_score > negative_score
                wins += 0.5 * (positive_score == negative_score)
        numerator += positives * wins / (positives * negatives)
        denominator += positives
    return numerator / denominator if denominator else 0.5


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--contract-check", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with open(args.config, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        config = json.load(handle)
    splits = load(args.data_dir, max_rows_per_split=64 if args.contract_check else None)
    encoded, dimension = encode(splits)
    train_features, train_labels, _ = encoded["train"]
    valid_features, valid_labels, valid_users = encoded["valid"]
    test_features, test_labels, _ = encoded["test"]
    model = Model(
        dimension,
        learning_rate=config["learning_rate"],
        l2=config["l2"],
    )
    if args.contract_check:
        probe_size = min(8, len(train_labels))
        if probe_size == 0 or len(valid_labels) == 0:
            raise ValueError("contract probe requires non-empty train and validation slices")
        loss = model.step(train_features[:probe_size], train_labels[:probe_size])
        probe_scores = model.predict(valid_features[:probe_size])
        if probe_scores.ndim != 1 or len(probe_scores) != min(probe_size, len(valid_features)):
            raise ValueError("model prediction shape violates the interface contract")
        if not np.isfinite(loss) or not np.all(np.isfinite(probe_scores)):
            raise ValueError("model produced NaN or infinity during contract probe")
        print(json.dumps({"contract": "ok", "feature_shape": list(train_features.shape)}))
        return
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config["seed"])
    best_score, best_state, stale = -1.0, None, 0
    for epoch in range(1, config["max_epochs"] + 1):
        order = rng.permutation(len(train_labels))
        losses = []
        for index in range(0, len(order), config["batch_size"]):
            batch = order[index:index + config["batch_size"]]
            losses.append(model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch]))
        predictions = model.predict(valid_features)
        proxy = within_user_auc(valid_users, valid_labels, predictions)
        print(f"epoch={epoch} loss={np.mean(losses):.6f} valid_gauc_proxy={proxy:.6f}")
        if proxy > best_score + 1e-5:
            best_score, best_state, stale = proxy, model.state(), 0
        else:
            stale += 1
            if stale >= config["patience"]:
                break
    if best_state is None:
        raise RuntimeError("training produced no checkpoint")
    model.load_state(best_state)
    np.savez(
        args.output,
        row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_labels), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(valid_features),
    )
    np.savez(
        Path(args.output).with_name("predictions_test.npz"),
        row_ids=np.arange(len(test_labels), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(test_features),
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Low-rank user-video interaction model with categorical residuals."""

import numpy as np


def sigmoid(value):
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(value, -30, 30)))


class Model:
    def __init__(self, dimension, learning_rate=0.01, l2=1e-6):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
        self.user_embeddings = rng.normal(
            0.0, 0.01, size=(dimension, 16)
        ).astype(np.float32)
        self.video_embeddings = rng.normal(
            0.0, 0.01, size=(dimension, 16)
        ).astype(np.float32)
        self.residual_weights = np.zeros(dimension, dtype=np.float32)
        self.bias = np.float32(0.0)
        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        self.l2 = l2

        self.user_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        self.user_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        self.video_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        self.video_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        self.residual_first_moment = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)
        self.residual_second_moment = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)
        self.step_number = 0

    @staticmethod
    def _normalized_interaction(user_vectors, video_vectors):
        epsilon = np.float32(1e-8)
        user_norms = np.sqrt((user_vectors * user_vectors).sum(axis=1) + epsilon)
        video_norms = np.sqrt((video_vectors * video_vectors).sum(axis=1) + epsilon)
        user_hat = user_vectors / user_norms[:, None]
        video_hat = video_vectors / video_norms[:, None]
        dots = (user_hat * video_hat).sum(axis=1)
        return dots, user_hat, video_hat, user_norms, video_norms

    def logits(self, features):
        user_vectors = self.user_embeddings[features[:, 0]]
        video_vectors = self.video_embeddings[features[:, 1]]
        interaction, _, _, _, _ = self._normalized_interaction(
            user_vectors, video_vectors
        )
        residual = self.residual_weights[features[:, 2:5]].sum(axis=1)
        return self.bias + interaction + residual

    def _adam_update(self, parameter, gradient, first_moment, second_moment):
        beta1, beta2, epsilon = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
        first_moment *= beta1
        first_moment += (1 - beta1) * gradient
        second_moment *= beta2
        second_moment += (1 - beta2) * (gradient * gradient)
        first_hat = first_moment / (1 - beta1 ** self.step_number)
        second_hat = second_moment / (1 - beta2 ** self.step_number)
        parameter -= self.learning_rate * first_hat / (np.sqrt(second_hat) + epsilon)

    def step(self, features, labels):
        size = len(labels)
        user_ids = features[:, 0]
        video_ids = features[:, 1]
        residual_ids = features[:, 2:5]

        user_vectors = self.user_embeddings[user_ids]
        video_vectors = self.video_embeddings[video_ids]
        interaction, user_hat, video_hat, user_norms, video_norms = (
            self._normalized_interaction(user_vectors, video_vectors)
        )
        residual = self.residual_weights[residual_ids].sum(axis=1)
        logits = self.bias + interaction + residual
        probabilities = sigmoid(logits)
        gradient = ((probabilities - labels) / size).astype(np.float32)

        grad_user_embeddings = np.zeros_like(self.user_embeddings)
        grad_video_embeddings = np.zeros_like(self.video_embeddings)
        grad_residual_weights = np.zeros_like(self.residual_weights)

        user_gradient = gradient[:, None] * (
            video_hat - interaction[:, None] * user_hat
        ) / user_norms[:, None]
        video_gradient = gradient[:, None] * (
            user_hat - interaction[:, None] * video_hat
        ) / video_norms[:, None]
        np.add.at(grad_user_embeddings, user_ids, user_gradient)
        np.add.at(grad_video_embeddings, video_ids, video_gradient)
        np.add.at(
            grad_residual_weights,
            residual_ids.ravel(),
            np.repeat(gradient, residual_ids.shape[1]),
        )

        grad_user_embeddings += self.l2 * self.user_embeddings
        grad_video_embeddings += self.l2 * self.video_embeddings
        grad_residual_weights += self.l2 * self.residual_weights

        self.step_number += 1
        self._adam_update(
            self.user_embeddings,
            grad_user_embeddings,
            self.user_first_moment,
            self.user_second_moment,
        )
        self._adam_update(
            self.video_embeddings,
            grad_video_embeddings,
            self.video_first_moment,
            self.video_second_moment,
        )
        self._adam_update(
            self.residual_weights,
            grad_residual_weights,
            self.residual_first_moment,
            self.residual_second_moment,
        )
        self.bias -= self.learning_rate * gradient.sum()

        return float(-np.mean(
            labels * np.log(probabilities + 1e-9)
            + (1 - labels) * np.log(1 - probabilities + 1e-9)
        ))

    def predict(self, features, batch_size=200_000):
        if len(features) == 0:
            return np.empty(0, dtype=np.float32)
        return np.concatenate([
            self.logits(features[index:index + batch_size])
            for index in range(0, len(features), batch_size)
        ])

    def state(self):
        return (
            self.user_embeddings.copy(),
            self.video_embeddings.copy(),
            self.residual_weights.copy(),
            np.float32(self.bias),
        )

    def load_state(self, state):
        user_embeddings, video_embeddings, residual_weights, bias = state
        self.user_embeddings = np.asarray(user_embeddings, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self.video_embeddings = np.asarray(video_embeddings, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self.residual_weights = np.asarray(residual_weights, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self.bias = np.float32(bias)

"""Train the neutral seed scaffold and emit validation scores for fixed evaluation."""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from data import encode, load
from model import Model


def within_user_auc(user_ids, labels, scores):
    """Training-only early-stop proxy; final scoring is owned by the Experimentor."""
    grouped = {}
    for user, label, score in zip(user_ids, labels, scores):
        grouped.setdefault(str(user), []).append((float(score), int(label)))
    numerator = denominator = 0.0
    for rows in grouped.values():
        positives = sum(label for _, label in rows)
        negatives = len(rows) - positives
        if positives == 0 or negatives == 0:
            continue
        wins = 0.0
        for positive_score, label in rows:
            if not label:
                continue
            for negative_score, other_label in rows:
                if other_label:
                    continue
                wins += positive_score > negative_score
                wins += 0.5 * (positive_score == negative_score)
        numerator += positives * wins / (positives * negatives)
        denominator += positives
    return numerator / denominator if denominator else 0.5


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--contract-check", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with open(args.config, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        config = json.load(handle)
    splits = load(args.data_dir, max_rows_per_split=64 if args.contract_check else None)
    encoded, dimension = encode(splits)
    train_features, train_labels, _ = encoded["train"]
    valid_features, valid_labels, valid_users = encoded["valid"]
    test_features, _ = encoded["test"]
    model = Model(
        dimension,
        learning_rate=config["learning_rate"],
        l2=config["l2"],
    )
    if args.contract_check:
        probe_size = min(8, len(train_labels))
        if probe_size == 0 or len(valid_labels) == 0:
            raise ValueError("contract probe requires non-empty train and validation slices")
        loss = model.step(train_features[:probe_size], train_labels[:probe_size])
        probe_scores = model.predict(valid_features[:probe_size])
        if probe_scores.ndim != 1 or len(probe_scores) != min(probe_size, len(valid_features)):
            raise ValueError("model prediction shape violates the interface contract")
        if not np.isfinite(loss) or not np.all(np.isfinite(probe_scores)):
            raise ValueError("model produced NaN or infinity during contract probe")
        print(json.dumps({"contract": "ok", "feature_shape": list(train_features.shape)}))
        return
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config["seed"])
    best_score, best_state, stale = -1.0, None, 0
    for epoch in range(1, config["max_epochs"] + 1):
        order = rng.permutation(len(train_labels))
        losses = []
        for index in range(0, len(order), config["batch_size"]):
            batch = order[index:index + config["batch_size"]]
            losses.append(model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch]))
        predictions = model.predict(valid_features)
        proxy = within_user_auc(valid_users, valid_labels, predictions)
        print(f"epoch={epoch} loss={np.mean(losses):.6f} valid_gauc_proxy={proxy:.6f}")
        if proxy > best_score + 1e-5:
            best_score, best_state, stale = proxy, model.state(), 0
        else:
            stale += 1
            if stale >= config["patience"]:
                break
    if best_state is None:
        raise RuntimeError("training produced no checkpoint")
    model.load_state(best_state)
    output_dir = Path(args.output)
    np.savez(
        output_dir.with_name("predictions_valid.npz"),
        row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_features), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(valid_features),
    )
    np.savez(
        output_dir.with_name("predictions_test.npz"),
        row_ids=np.arange(len(test_features), dtype=np.int64),
        scores=model.predict(test_features),
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Supplied KuaiRand-Pure files and official splits

## Summary and mechanism
The supplied data directory has three 19-column impression logs and three entity tables. ParLLiaMent's
official temporal split uses standard-exposure rows: train 2022-04-08 through 2022-04-21, validation
2022-04-22 through 2022-04-28, and test 2022-04-29 through 2022-05-08.

## When to use / avoid
Use this inventory before choosing data sources or defining temporal features. Avoid treating file
boundaries as split boundaries: the later standard log contains both validation and test dates.
Avoid treating the random-exposure file as official validation or test data.

## Requirements and implementation
Measured directly from the supplied CSVs: `log_standard_4_08_to_4_21_pure.csv` has 1,141,112 rows
covering 2022-04-09 through 2022-04-21; `log_standard_4_22_to_5_08_pure.csv` has 295,497 rows over 17
dates. Date filtering yields 124,909 validation rows and 170,588 test rows. The random log has
1,186,059 rows over 2022-04-22 through 2022-05-08. Entity tables contain 27,285 users and 7,583
videos, with one row per ID.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Read standard logs in source order, select rows by integer `date`, and preserve that order for
validation inference. Fit encoders and transforms on training only. Use explicit unknown buckets for
entities or values absent from training.

## Diagnostics and risks
The nominal train range includes April 8, but this supplied training file's observed minimum date is
April 9. Hard-coding expected daily row counts or concatenating all standard rows before fitting can
silently leak validation/test information. File names alone do not establish feature availability.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Before a run, assert filenames, headers, row counts, observed date bounds, unique IDs, and the exact
124,909-row validation selection. Fingerprint inputs so cached screening is invalidated after a data
change.

## Related cards and sources
See `dataset.interaction_log_schema`, `dataset.user_metadata`,
`dataset.video_metadata_and_statistics`, `dataset.random_exposure_log`, and
`task.prediction_artifact`. Counts were measured from the supplied KuaiRand-Pure CSVs; split rules
come from ParLLiaMent's fixed evaluator.
research_knowledge_base.title: Supplied KuaiRand-Pure files and official splits

# Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics

## Summary and mechanism
GAUC summarizes per-user positive-negative ordering with positive-count weighting; nDCG@5 emphasizes
discounted relevance at the top five. Primary averages them.

## When to use / avoid
Use official metrics for selection and stopping. Use accuracy, precision, recall, F1, global AUC,
average precision, MAP@5, MRR@5, and HitRate@5 only to diagnose mechanisms.

## Requirements and implementation
Preserve canonical rows and group only inside fixed evaluation. Compare every change with its exact
parent and inspect segment support before interpreting deltas.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
No metric reweighting is permitted. A hypothesis should predict GAUC and nDCG@5 separately because
loss and sampling changes can trade them off.

## Diagnostics and risks
Validation-selected classification thresholds are optimistic. Score scaling can change thresholded
metrics without changing rank; zero-positive users make macro top-k metrics harsh but defined.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Run synthetic perfect, tied, all-negative, and non-finite cases before trusting evaluator changes.

## Related cards and sources
See `task.kuairand_ranking` and `experiment.scarce_budget`.
research_knowledge_base.title: Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics

research_knowledge_base.content:
# Counted-experiment and convergence protocol

## Summary and mechanism
ParLLiaMent has a scarce budget of at most 50 successfully scored experiments. The selected seed scaffold
is unscored parent 0. It may be the fresh simple scaffold or the optional KuaiRand FM baseline code,
but neither selection inserts a measured baseline result. Train-only screening, planning, failed
retries, and abandoned attempts do not receive experiment IDs or consume the counted budget.

## When to use / avoid
Use this card whenever prioritizing hypotheses or interpreting lineage. Prefer one high-information,
bounded change over broad searches. Avoid citing parent 0 as measured evidence, treating an
abandoned attempt as an experiment, or spending official experiments on basic schema discovery.

## Requirements and implementation
Only a successful validation score atomically becomes `experiment_N` and enters the Journal.
Generated candidates must reference parent 0 or an actually scored experiment available in the
current archive. One tournament winner proceeds to implementation per generation, even when draft
planning considered a larger candidate portfolio.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Before an official experiment, use the cached train-only temporal screen, literature, prior metrics,
and segment diagnostics to state one exact ablation and an expected effect on both GAUC and nDCG@5.
Reserve official scoring for changes with a plausible primary gain and a clean fallback.

## Diagnostics and risks
Every scored experiment with primary score `x` establishes a target of `x + 0.002`. ParLLiaMent stops if
all three subsequent scored experiments are strictly below that target, so the check requires at
least four scored experiments. Reaching the target in any of those three experiments prevents that
anchor from causing convergence. Abandoned attempts are absent from this sequence. The globally
highest-scoring validation experiment is selected for submission even when a later, lower-scoring
experiment triggers convergence. Repeated implementation failures waste wall-clock time despite
being uncounted.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Use profiling, train-only temporal holdout screening, contract checks, and code validation before
training. Then change the smallest coherent set of files needed for the winning hypothesis and
compare it against its declared scored parent.

## Related cards and sources
See `task.kuairand_ranking`, `task.prediction_artifact`, and
`evaluation.within_user_metrics`. The authoritative source is `parlliament_mle_plan.md` plus the
implemented Journal and Overseer convergence checks.
research_knowledge_base.title: Counted-experiment and convergence protocol

research_knowledge_base.content:
# KuaiRand within-user long-view ranking

## Summary and mechanism
The task scores the already logged impressions for each user; it is not full-catalog retrieval.
`long_view` is binary relevance. The official `primary` score is
`(GAUC + nDCG@5) / 2`, and it is the only experiment-selection and convergence objective.

## When to use / avoid
Use this card to reject changes that improve row calibration without changing within-user order.
Avoid treating the unscored seed or a user-only constant as a performance baseline.

## Requirements and implementation
Predictions must preserve canonical validation row order and contain one finite score per row. A
useful model must vary scores among a user's candidate items. GAUC is the positive-count-weighted
mean of per-user AUC over users containing both classes. nDCG@5 is macro-averaged over every user;
users with no positive impression receive zero nDCG.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Always report GAUC, nDCG@5, and primary separately. Optimize ordering, not a validation-selected
classification threshold. Classification and supplementary ranking metrics are diagnostic only.

## Diagnostics and risks
Global AUC can rise while GAUC stalls. Zero-positive users contribute zero nDCG but do not provide
within-user positive-negative AUC evidence. User-only constants cannot change within-user order;
user features need to interact with an item, author, context, or history signal to affect the score.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Before training, verify score variance within user and the exact prediction artifact contract. Test
one ranking-relevant change against a scored parent.

## Related cards and sources
See `task.experiment_protocol`, `task.prediction_artifact`,
`dataset.population_and_pair_shift`, and `evaluation.within_user_metrics`. Task details are fixed by
ParLLiaMent's immutable evaluator; dataset context is Gao et al., “KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential
Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos” (2022).
research_knowledge_base.title: KuaiRand within-user long-view ranking

research_knowledge_base.content:
# Impression-time availability and leakage policy

## Summary and mechanism
A feature is eligible only when its value would be known before ranking the target impression.
Historical aggregates must exclude the current label and all future events.

## When to use / avoid
Use timestamps, request context, and causally accumulated histories. Avoid current-impression
outcomes, official-validation-derived fitting, future histories, and snapshots lacking availability
timestamps.

## Requirements and implementation
Sort training events by time, compute features from prior state, then update state after emitting the
row. Fit vocabularies, thresholds, and transforms on training data only. Treat engagement columns
such as `is_click`, `play_time_ms`, and `long_view` as post-impression outcomes for the current row.
Treat the video-statistics snapshot as unavailable until its observation window is established.

## Starting configuration and expected effects
Default unknown values explicitly and monitor coverage. Leakage can create implausibly large gains
in both GAUC and nDCG@5 that disappear under a temporal split.

## Diagnostics and risks
Warning signs are near-perfect metrics, cold rows outperforming warm rows unexpectedly, or gains
concentrated in post-event fields.

## Cheapest check and clean experiment
Perturb the current label and other current outcomes and verify the row's engineered features do not
change. Run the internal temporal holdout before an official experiment.

## Related cards and sources
See `dataset.interaction_log_schema`, `dataset.video_metadata_and_statistics`,
`features.causal_histories`, and `robustness.temporal_drift`.
research_knowledge_base.title: Impression-time availability and leakage policy

ranking.rationale: string

Best evidence-to-scope trade-off. It extends the only positively screened feature family with one bounded interaction, targets a large weak tab-0 cohort, preserves the strong additive architecture, and has low leakage and runtime risk. User-by-tab sparsity remains material, so the expected gain should be treated as modest rather than established.

A highly constrained, low-cost correction to checkpoint selection: it aligns early stopping with the stated primary metric rather than optimizing only GAUC. It is preferable to nDCG-only selection because it preserves the official GAUC/nDCG trade-off. Main penalty is validation-selection overfitting from choosing among many checkpoints on the same validation set.

Directly aligns training with the within-user GAUC component and is meaningfully distinct from feature crosses. The failed low-rank architecture does not refute a loss-only change to the winning additive model. It is penalized for medium runtime, pair-sampling implementation risk, and uncertain nDCG@5 benefit.

Video-by-weekday is the lowest-sparsity video-context interaction proposed and stays within the screened request-context family. It is a clean one-feature ablation with low operational risk, but evidence is indirect and the video-by-weekday cells may still be sparse under temporal shift.

Conservative regularization test on the best model is cheap, isolated, and defensible after the more flexible embedding model failed badly. The downside is weak direct evidence that current additive weights are overfit, and the proposed tenfold L2 change is still a hyperparameter probe with likely small effect.

A safe convergence check with existing early stopping protection and no feature or leakage expansion. However, it is weakly motivated, partially redundant with the existing training procedure, and can consume additional runtime without evidence that ten epochs is insufficient.

Video-by-tab has a plausible surface-conditional relevance rationale and targets tab heterogeneity, including the sizable tab-6 slice. It is ranked below video-by-weekday because video-by-tab cells are likely sparse and the low tab metrics are diagnostic slices, not causal evidence that this interaction will generalize.

A bounded train-fitted interaction using eligible request time, but the rationale rests heavily on one small hour-3 slice with only 1,284 rows. User-by-hour is also likely less stable over time than user-by-tab and has limited expected aggregate impact.

Low cost but dominated by c08: nDCG-only checkpoint selection misaligns with the official primary metric while retaining the same validation checkpoint-selection overfitting risk. It is effectively a narrower, less well-aligned duplicate of the official-primary selection candidate.

Targets the nDCG@5 weakness, but combines a new pairwise loss, rank-dependent dynamic weighting, and direct tailoring to validation diagnostics. This creates substantial validation-overfitting and implementation risk, can sacrifice GAUC, and is too complex for the single scarce experiment relative to c05.

Video-by-hour has the highest expected cell sparsity among feature-cross proposals and its rationale depends on weak hour slices rather than robust training evidence. The stated confidence of 10 is not supported by its own uncertainty range or the evidence, further reducing credibility.

Clean and cheap, but it has no evidence-specific mechanism, predicts zero primary gain, and changing learning rate under a fixed epoch budget may simply undertrain. It is the weakest use of a scarce experiment.

system: Rank every proposed recommender candidate head-to-head for one scarce experiment. Penalize weak evidence, duplication, validation overfitting, leakage, excessive scope, and runtime risk. Ranking position 1 is best. Return only one valid JSON object. Do not use Markdown fences.

expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by 0.000 to +0.003 if timing-specific video effects improve rank placement among same-user candidates.

candidates.rationale: The observed hour-level ranking variation leaves open a content availability or audience-timing effect. This is a bounded interaction among already used impression-time fields, rather than a new metadata family rejected by screening.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, replace pointwise BCE with a within-user sampled pairwise logistic loss using only each training user's positive and negative impressions; keep the additive model, all features, optimizer hyperparameters, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.004 because optimization is aligned directly to within-user positive-negative ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.003 because pairwise sampling may improve broad ordering without reliably emphasizing rank five.

candidates.rationale: The official objective is entirely within-user ranking, and experiment 1 already provides the strongest observed score. A pairwise loss directly trains the positive-versus-negative ordering that defines GAUC, while preserving the successful additive representation.
candidates.text: Replace pointwise BCE with a within-user pairwise logistic ranking loss.

candidates.exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 1, replace pointwise BCE with a within-user pairwise logistic loss whose sampled pair weight is larger when the positive item's current predicted rank is near or below five; keep the additive model, features, optimizer hyperparameters, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.002 to +0.002 because top-rank weighting can sacrifice lower-rank pair ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.005 if weighted updates promote relevant items around the top-five cutoff.

candidates.rationale: Experiment 2 shows a meaningful separation between GAUC and nDCG@5 in tab 6 and medium-frequency items. Weighting pairwise errors by the current predicted rank targets the metric's known top-five weakness rather than adding unsupported features.
candidates.text: Replace pointwise BCE with a top-five-weighted within-user pairwise logistic loss.
